Where it began

Beau Webster was born in Hobart on 1 December 1993 and grew up in Snug, in the south of Tasmania, playing his junior cricket for the Kingborough club. He came through the Tasmania Under-23 side and made his first-class debut for the state against Queensland at Hobart in February 2014.

For some years he was best known as a batter who bowled a little off-spin. When he captained a Cricket Australia XI in the 2017–18 one-day competition, he opened the campaign with 121 against South Australia, his first List A hundred, and helped that side to only the second win it had ever recorded.

The player

The 2023–24 Sheffield Shield season was the one that made people sit up. He made 938 runs, took 30 wickets and was named player of the series. Only Garfield Sobers had reached 900 runs and 30 wickets in a single Shield season before him.

Australia first called him into the Test squad in November 2024, as cover for Mitchell Marsh. His debut came at Sydney in January 2025, against India, and his fifty was the only one in either side's first innings. In the World Test Championship final that June he made 72 from 92 balls when batting was hard work for everyone. Left out of the first four Tests of the 2025–26 Ashes, he came back for the last one, again at Sydney, and made 71 not out. By November 2026 he had played 12 Tests, with 533 runs at 31.35 including five fifties, 12 wickets at 32.33 with a best of 3 for 64, and 16 catches.

What made him special

Two bowlers for the price of one. In 2020, during the first COVID-19 lockdown, he decided to learn medium pace, using his height to get extra bounce. By the 2020–21 Shield season he could switch between seam and off-spin as the day required, and comparisons with Colin Miller and Andrew Symonds followed. His bowling could win a game on its own, too: in a one-day match in October 2024 he took 6 for 17 against Western Australia, who lost eight wickets for a single run while he was bowling.

By November 2026 a Test hundred had not yet come his way, though he had twice got within thirty runs of one. That sort of thing has a habit of sorting itself out.

Away from the middle

He has taken his game well beyond Tasmania. At home he has played Big Bash cricket for the Hobart Hurricanes. In England he had a spell with Essex in the 2023 One-Day Cup, finishing as their top run-scorer and top wicket-taker, and later signed for Gloucestershire for 2024 and for three months with Warwickshire in 2025.

And finally

Plenty of people took up something new during lockdown, from bread-making to jigsaws, and most of it was quietly put away afterwards. Webster took up a second bowling style, kept it, and bowled it in Test cricket. Few people have spent their time indoors more usefully.
